evidence.quote: Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch
In our loop a Codex agent writes extra operations for the model, as Python code built on move_eef , together with a guide on when to use them.
In each round the model runs the current library on one group, and the agent then reviews those runs, with their scores, action logs and videos, and revises the library for the next round.
Unlike the demonstrations, the library is not stored or looked up by task, and every task sees the same operations and the same guide.
Demonstrations and a self-written skill library change how the model acts, but neither clearly beats the default, and both make an episode more expensive.
They also draw on the tasks being scored, so their scores are not comparable with a standard evaluation.
Each round runs on a different group, so the group results are not a learning curve.
All experiments run in simulation, on one benchmark and with one model, and each configuration is run once on the evaluation set.
